title: Crispy Maple Eggs
subtitle: Cottage cheese and egg batter for a high-protein griddle classic.
description: Blended cottage cheese in the custard adds protein without chalky protein powder. Thick-cut bread soaks briefly, griddles to a crisp shell, and serves with berries and maple for a crew that wants comfort food with staying power.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.notes: plus 1 tsp vanilla and pinch of cinnamon

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Crispy Maple Eggs in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Blend the batter
steps.instruction: Blend cottage cheese, eggs, milk, vanilla, cinnamon, and maple until completely smooth—no curds. Pour into a shallow hotel pan for fast dipping. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Heat the griddle
steps.instruction: Heat a large griddle or cast iron over medium. Add butter until foaming but not brown. Work in batches so slices aren't crowded. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Soak and griddle
steps.instruction: Dip bread 3–4 seconds per side—don't oversaturate or centers stay raw. Griddle 3 minutes per side until deep golden and custard sets; adjust heat if browning too fast. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold warm
steps.instruction: Transfer finished slices to a wire rack on a sheet pan in a 200°F oven. Uncovered keeps the crust; cover only if holding longer than 20 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Plate and serve
steps.instruction: Stack two slices per plate, top with berries and a drizzle of maple. Offer Greek yogurt for extra protein without slowing the line. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Blend batter first and keep the dip pan shallow so slices don't over-soak during rush assembly.
One cook griddles while another plates berries and maple—sync batches to two slices per firefighter.
Use a wire rack for holding; stacking hot French toast steams the crust soft before service.
cleanupNotes: Rinse the blender immediately with warm water before cottage cheese dries on the blade assembly.
Scrape the griddle while warm with a bench scraper, then wipe with a butter-damp towel.
leftovers: Reheat slices on a sheet pan at 325°F for 8 minutes directly on the rack for a crisp re-crisp.
Chop cold slices into a bread pudding base with extra eggs, milk, and raisins for tomorrow's bake.
